campaign.title: The Discovery Below
campaign.subtitle: A Fulminary Prologue
campaign.description: Theron, an elven Edenite miner, learns that the stone his city sells has been holding something down. A branching prologue of family, industry and restrained horror beneath Sturmvale.

S04.title: The Face Comes Apart
S04.objective: Stabilize the western cut long enough to choose what can still be saved.
S04.stakes: Every failed approach costs health. Four rounds of danger pass before the collapse decides for you.
S04.success_text: You read the collapse before it finishes happening. The crew has seconds—and seconds are enough.
S04.failure_text: The face wins the argument. You crawl clear carrying injuries, incomplete answers, and no clean version of what happened.

success_effects.notice: The Crownvein crew will remember this.

S05.title: The Borrowed Voice
S05.objective: Map the chamber while something beneath it tries to make you answer.
S05.stakes: The room rewards attention and punishes recognition. Exposure rises when it gets inside your guard.
S05.success_text: The impossible geometry resolves into a pattern: not a prison wall, but a seal whose pieces have been sold away.
S05.failure_text: You leave with only fragments of the pattern—and the certainty that the voice now knows which memories open you fastest.

S08.title: Ground the Impossible
S08.objective: Complete Timinny's circuit without letting the charged fragment complete one through you.
S08.stakes: Careful work yields a tool for the final descent. A failed experiment leaves only theory and additional exposure.
S08.success_text: The current crosses copper, stone, and earth in a repeatable sequence. Timinny has a device; you have a method.
S08.failure_text: The apparatus burns out before the final reading. The principle is sound, but you will descend without a finished ground.

success_effects.notice: Timinny's grounding coil added to your equipment.

failure_effects.notice: Residual charge settles into the stormscar.

actions.label: Work the hair-thin leads

S09.title: Make the Record Hold
S09.objective: Force the Commission to confront evidence it has already decided is inconvenient.
S09.stakes: This is a contest over credibility, not truth. Failure costs health as strain and hardens the Commission's response.
S09.success_text: For one dangerous minute the chamber stops treating you like a miner who wandered into policy and starts treating you like a witness.
S09.failure_text: The commissioners convert every warning into a procedural flaw. You keep the truth, but lose the room.

success_effects.notice: Your warning reaches someone beyond the Commission.

failure_effects.notice: The Commission marks Theron as disruptive.

S13.title: The Mine Turns Hostile
S13.objective: Reach the central descent while the broken galleries rearrange around the incursion.
S13.stakes: The enemy is pressure, falling stone, and a thing that learns voices. Survive five exchanges and keep the route open.
S13.success_text: You do not defeat what came through. You deny it the shape of a victory and reach the broken seal ahead of the collapse.
S13.failure_text: The mine takes blood and time from you. The route remains barely possible, but someone else pays for the delay.

actions.description: Move on the darkness between pulses and carry a grounding line across the open shaft.

S14.title: Reconstruct the Edenite Seal
S14.objective: Restore a working circuit from a barrier the city has spent generations dismantling.
S14.stakes: This is the decisive challenge. Progress must outrun the breach; failure still closes the chamber, but at a far greater personal cost.
S14.success_text: The last shard seats. Edenite answers Edenite, lightning finds earth, and the emptiness below is forced back behind a shape it remembers.
S14.failure_text: The improvised seal closes by consuming every margin you left it—blood, memory, and the unbroken parts of your body. It holds. Barely.

codex.title: Edenite Fracture
codex.body: Fresh Edenite does not merely carry storm charge. Under stress it redirects force along boundaries that resemble deliberate joins rather than natural crystal faults.

codex.title: Barrier Geometry
codex.body: The black chamber is bounded by an incomplete circular network. Intact Edenite ends every scorched vein. The extracted mineral was part of the boundary itself.

codex.title: The Grounding Principle
codex.body: Edenite charge can be redirected through a sequenced copper-and-stone circuit. The current seeks continuity before it seeks the shortest path.

codex.title: The Crownvein Hearing
codex.body: Theron's warning entered the EMC record as an allegation of structural discontinuity, anomalous conduction, and unsafe extraction. Its language was narrowed, but it existed.

codex.title: Borrowed Voices
codex.body: The presence below does not imitate voices at random. It selects familiar speech, imperfectly understood but precisely timed, to pull listeners off safe routes.

codex.title: The Edenite Seal
codex.body: Sturmvale's mineral wealth was a distributed containment system. Buildings, treatments, and exports did not consume a resource; they dismantled a lock.

epilogue_blocks.content: Varrik gave his statement with one arm strapped across his chest and no softness anywhere in it. He had ordered the cut. He said so twice, so no clerk could mishear it.
Theron's warning entered the record beside the order that ignored it. It changed nothing that had already happened, and everything that could be argued afterward.

scenes.title: A Roof That Remembers
scenes.subtitle: Bethella's home, before dawn
scenes.author_notes: Fixed event: family established. visual_brief: A modest elven home in Sturmvale before dawn. Pale stone, dark timber, narrow windows, faintly luminous Edenite braces in repaired roof joints. Theron secures a mining satchel; Edran studies rolled mine maps; Bethella sits beneath a blanket, alert but affected by stormlung. Threatening clouds beyond the glass. No demonic imagery. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

entry_effects.notice: Theron's years reading stone sharpen his Wits.
Main quest begun: What the Stone Holds

blocks.content: The roof always knew the storm before the sky did.

Its oldest beams complained first, groaning softly over the kitchen as if roused from an uneasy sleep. A breath later a pale blue shimmer moved through the western joints — there and gone so quickly it might have been moonlight, except that dawn had not yet found Sturmvale.
Theron looked up from the buckle of his mining satchel.

The house had survived three generations of weather and two of repairs, though survival had left it with little dignity. Its walls were the pale local stone of western Fulminary; its rafters dark timber, smoke-stained and bowed. Where the roof had split the winter before, Theron had packed the seams with mason’s compound mixed with powdered Edenite. Worked into mortar, the precious mineral could scarcely be seen — which was precisely the point. In Sturmvale, Edenite was not ornament. It lived inside bridge piers, retaining walls, infirmary splints, and the bones of old houses whose owners could not afford to rebuild them.
It was the reason the city still stood beneath its increasingly violent skies. It was also the reason Theron spent most of his waking life underground.
There goes the western brace again — twice now, and the sun's not even up. It flashes at me like it means to say something, and in thirty years I've never once worked out what.

Bethella was Theron’s mother, though strangers sometimes mistook her for his elder sister. Elves aged slowly, and illness had thinned her without yet making her look old. A wool blanket covered her knees. One hand rested around a cup that had long since stopped steaming; the other lay near the small silver clasp at her collar, where a sliver of Edenite no larger than a fingernail had been set.
It likes the attention. Set a scrap of Edenite in a wall and it spends the rest of its life reminding you it's in there.
You're the one who packed it into the seam. If it's showing off, it learned that from the man who put it there.

That was Edran, Theron’s younger brother — twenty-four, earnest in all the places Theron had learned to be guarded, and presently losing a battle against three maps, a heel of bread, and an ink pot set much too near his elbow.
Which is exactly how I know it's only showing off. If it were truly failing it wouldn't bother with the theatrics — it'd just go dark and leave the roof to explain the rest.
You told me it would last through winter. You said it with the very same face you're wearing now, which is how I've learned not to trust either one.
It did last the winter. I was careful to specify which winter.
It's summer, Theron. Has been for a month. Even the stone's worked that out.
Then we've exceeded expectations, and I'd sooner not press a brace that's already outlived its own promise.
The two of you would bicker over a burning house and call it keeping busy. Some mornings I think it's the only reason the roof's still up — it wouldn't dare interrupt.

His mother’s laugh broke into a cough. It began lightly enough, then caught deep in her chest and would not leave. Theron crossed the kitchen before Edran could rise, steadying her cup with one hand while he touched the setting at her collar with the other. The Edenite was dim.

Stormlung had begun as a miner’s ailment generations ago, when stone dust and charged air scarred the breath. Now it took people who had never gone down a shaft. Physicians blamed the metallic rain, the pressure, the dust shaken loose whenever thunder rolled under a clear sky. They agreed on little except that properly prepared Edenite eased the spasms — provided one had enough of it.
Don't start fussing. I can hear you winding up to it from clear across the room — you get the same crease your father used to get, right there.
I haven't started fussing. This is the quiet part that comes before the fussing, where I pretend I'm only checking the clasp and you pretend you believe me.
Timinny's teaching you bad habits. You never used to hover. You used to just worry in silence and ruin your own breakfast over it, like a decent son.
In fairness, Timinny only taught him to label the bad habits. The habits themselves he came by honestly — from you.

Theron tilted the silver clasp toward the stove light. The fine veins within had gone almost colorless. It might last another week. It might fail that afternoon, if the storm broke hard. Bethella watched his face and, as mothers do, found the thought he had hoped to hide.
Well? You've had that clasp in the stove-light long enough to have formed an opinion. Out with it.

choices.choice_text: "I'll bring home enough for a proper setting this time. No more scraps."
tags: outcome:Theron gives Bethella a promise he is not certain the mine will let him keep.

choices.choice_text: "If the roof does come down, at least Edran's maps can tell us where it landed."
tags: outcome:The joke buys a breath of normality. Bethella hears the worry beneath it anyway.

choices.choice_text: "The charge is building faster than it should. Do me a favor — stay off the western wall today."

scenes.title: The Things Stone Can Do
scenes.subtitle: Timinny's workshop
scenes.author_notes: Fixed event: grounding behaviour first observed. Includes the S01 tone payoff, the map setup and the treatment beat. visual_brief: A crowded engineering workshop of bridge models, stone braces, copper leads and mineral samples; Timinny in a rugged self-built wheeled chair; Theron kneeling at a miniature stone arch braced by three blue-white Edenite fragments; storm-dark window backlight. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: Theron released the clasp only after its light steadied. As he straightened, a red wax crest on Edran’s uppermost map caught his eye — a crown divided by a descending line. Beneath it, in precise Commission lettering: CROWNVEIN — LOWER EXPANSION.
That shouldn't be here, Edran. Not on our table, not under the butter, not anywhere a man could set a cup of tea down on it.
Good morning to you too. I sleep four hours, walk home in the dark, and the first thing my brother wants to discuss is where my own paperwork is permitted to sit.
Crownvein surveys don't leave the EMC archive. They hardly leave the room the archive is in — a man signs three ledgers just to look at one. And here it is, keeping company with your breakfast.

Everyone in Sturmvale knew the initials. The Edenite Mining Commission licensed every legal shaft in Fulminary, set extraction quotas, and decided which walls were reinforced when the storms damaged more of the city than the season’s supply could mend. Crownvein was its newest undertaking and already its most valuable — a western mine sunk into a formation so rich the High Council had begun measuring its future in cartloads.
It's a training copy. Old measurements, no extraction marks, nothing they'd ever miss. Selwick hands them round to the juniors so we can make our mistakes on stone that's already been dug.

Edran worked as a junior stone-cartographer, which meant the Commission trusted him to copy the discoveries of better-paid surveyors without adding any of his own. The work suited his patience. It did not suit his imagination — though Edran had not yet decided whether he possessed one.
I've got to reconcile the western descent before second bell, or Selwick will spend another whole morning telling me my strata lines wander like a drunk hunting for his own front door.
They do wander. I've stood at your shoulder while you draw — you follow the stone to wherever it turns interesting, not to wherever it's actually going.
Stone's allowed to wander. It was down there folding and shifting for an age before the Commission ever decided the world owed it a straight line.
Stone's allowed to. Cartographers aren't. Selwick doesn't pay you to sympathize with the rock — he pays you to make it behave on paper.
One of these days I'll draw a thing exactly as it is, with nothing left for you to correct, and I honestly don't know what you'll do with yourself.

Theron leaned over the table. Near the bottom of the survey, the western descent curved around a pale crescent where the contour marks simply ceased. It was too smooth to be spilled ink and too deliberate to be damage.
What's this, though — here, at the bottom of the descent? The line just… stops. Everything's crowded with contour and then there's this pale nothing, smooth as a thumbprint pressed in wax.
Bad ink.
Bad ink usually has the decency to at least exist on the page. This is a hole shaped like somebody meant it.
It's a copying omission, Theron. Every survey carries a few — a patch the original surveyor left blank and no one after thought worth chasing down.
Not shaped like that, they don't. Omissions come out ragged. That's a clean curve. Someone's hand went around it on purpose and then thought better of writing down why.
You cut the stone, Theron. I'm the one who draws it. Let me keep the one thing in this house I'm meant to be the expert on.
Then draw that. Fill in your pale nothing, and let's see what shape the truth turns out to be once you've been honest with it.

For a moment Edran said nothing. His fingertip traced the blank curve without touching the parchment. Theron knew the small crease between his brows: his brother had noticed the anomaly before now — he had only lacked a name for it.
You'll miss Timinny if you keep cross-examining your brother over the breakfast things. That old man counts every minute you're late and charges you interest on all of them.
Beyond the narrow window the clouds had thickened into a single dark shelf over the western roofs. Timinny disliked tardiness on principle, particularly when Theron was the one practicing it.
Keep this one out — set it apart from the others. Don't roll it up with the morning's work and lose it back into the pile.
Why? What am I keeping it out for?
It's got bad ink.

At the door Theron paused to look back. Bethella had drawn the blanket closer. Edran was already bent over the Crownvein sheet, his breakfast forgotten. Between them stood a house held together by old timber, careful repairs, and trace amounts of the thing Theron was helping tear from the earth. He stepped into the cold morning.

Sturmvale fell away around him in steep streets and pale terraces, the mining capital rising from the Fulminary foothills like a city braced against an unseen hand. Copper lightning rods crowded the roofs. Drain channels crossed every lane. Far above, the High Council’s towers watched over districts that grew poorer the nearer they came to the mine lifts.

Somewhere beneath the western street, something struck stone three times. Theron stopped. The blows reached him through the soles of his boots — three, evenly spaced, too measured for settling foundations. A cart rattled around the corner; when it passed, the street was silent again. He waited. The sound did not repeat.

Timinny’s workshop contained three kinds of object: things that worked, things that might work, and things he insisted had been ruined by someone else’s measurements. Models of bridges hung from ceiling hooks. Copper leads crossed the walls in tangled lines. Stone braces, gear housings, mineral samples, and annotated failures competed for space on tables that had not held food in years. The room smelled of lamp oil, hot metal, and the bitter antiseptic paste Timinny pretended not to need.

Theron found the old inventor beneath a suspended bridge model, tightening a copper contact. Timinny was not, in truth, very old for an elf — pain had aged him more efficiently than time. A heavy blanket covered his legs, and his body sat within a rugged wheeled chair of his own design, all dark wood, brass joints, and stubbornly unnecessary improvements. Years earlier an infection called deepvein had entered through a workshop wound and settled into the nerves of his lower body. Edenite treatment had stopped its spread. It had not restored his legs. He had built the chair after dismissing every other model as an insult to wheels — and he had taught Theron that stone could be questioned, provided one learned to recognize its answers.
You're late. You're always late, and you always come through that door wearing the face of a man who believes being charming about it will somehow help.
I'm not late. I'm early for tomorrow. It's only ever a question of which day you choose to measure me against.
That joke was tired when I could still walk to the door and hold it open for you to leave through.
You laughed back then. I remember it distinctly. It was a small laugh, but it was mine and I earned it.
I could leave the room back then. A man will laugh at nearly anything while he's still got the option of walking away from it.
You still could laugh, you know. As it happens, I've brought you something worth it.

Theron took a small parcel from the false bottom of his satchel, its cloth singed at one corner, and set it on the clearest part of the bench — which required moving two calipers, a cracked lens, and something that looked distressingly like a mechanical finger. The humor left Timinny’s face the moment the cloth opened. The fragment was nothing like the pale commercial cuts sold to masons and physicians: its blue-white glow was dense enough to cast shadows, and a dark filament ran through its center like ink trapped beneath ice.
That's not waste stone. Don't insult the pair of us. I've handled a thousand cuts in this room and not one of them ever looked back at me.
It was going to be waste. Slated for the tailings, bound for the crusher. I only… moved it along before it got there.
Everything becomes waste if you steal it badly enough. 'Moved it along.' You've got your brother's gift for drawing a soft line around a hard fact.
Timinny rolled to the far table and swept a stack of drawings to the floor without apology. A miniature stone tower stood there, split from base to parapet, three shallow housings carved around it.
The southern piece first — there, into the brace. We'll put a question to it and see whether it's rude enough to answer.

Theron divided the fragments and seated them in the housings. Timinny connected each to a copper lead, then raised a vane through the workshop’s roof vent. Static had been gathering over Sturmvale since midnight; it traveled down the wire with a rising whine.
If this explodes and takes the roof with it, you understand Bethella will blame you, not the lightning.
If it explodes, cultivate the discipline not to tell her.

The discharge struck. White light snapped across the table — and instead of splitting the cracked model apart, the radiance passed from the first Edenite fragment into the second, then the third, traveling sideways around the break and sinking harmlessly into the base. The fracture remained, but its edges had drawn closer together.
It moved. You saw it — the charge went sideways, right around the break, as though it knew the crack was there and chose to spare it.
Energy moves. That is the entire occupation of energy. Don't go making a miracle of it before we've ruled out that it's merely strange.
Not like that, it doesn't. Charge takes the shortest road it can find. That took the one road that left the stone whole.
No. …No. Not like that.

For years Fulminary’s engineers had treated Edenite as a substance — crush it into mortar, set it against damaged flesh, place it where the pressure was greatest. What lay on the table suggested something else. The pieces had not acted alone. They had behaved as parts of a single arrangement. A system. Timinny lifted the fragment with padded forceps and turned it toward the window. The dark thread inside seemed to bend toward the storm.
Where did you get this, Theron? And think before you answer — I'm about to decide exactly how much trouble I'm willing to be in alongside you.

choices.choice_text: "The Crown. The new western face — it warmed before the thunder last shift. I took it before Varrik counted the cut."
tags: outcome:Timinny receives the whole truth and begins treating Theron as a partner rather than a source.

effects.notice: Timinny knows where the stone came from.

choices.choice_text: "A discarded cut. I didn't notice the dark thread until after I'd brought it out."
tags: impact:Keep part of the experiment hidden
outcome:Theron gives Timinny enough truth to continue and keeps the most dangerous part of it for himself.

choices.choice_text: "Are we looking at my employment here, or the impossible thing the stone just did?"
tags: outcome:Theron refuses the question. Timinny continues the experiment, but no longer assumes they are taking the same risk.

scenes.title: The New Cut
scenes.subtitle: Crownvein Mine
scenes.author_notes: Fixed event: Theron assigned to Crownvein. Opens with the treatment beat that closes S02. visual_brief: An immense mine staging floor with timber lifts, carved supports, wet rails, suspended lamps and carts of luminous Edenite; the EMC crest above the primary lift; Varrik broad and severe in a foreman's coat. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

entry_effects.notice: Quest updated: Inspect the new cut

blocks.content: Timinny returned the fragment to the cloth. As he did, his hand trembled — a small movement he tried to hide against the blanket. Theron’s gaze dropped to the metal housing fixed beside his hip, where a prepared Edenite core fed a low, steady charge into a web of fine contacts beneath his clothes. The treatment quieted the deepvein infection. Without it the pain returned first, then fever, then the slow upward creep of numbness. The core was almost colorless.
How long? And the true number this time — not the one you keep polished for visitors.
Four days. Five, perhaps, if I sit very still and give up enjoying myself entirely.
You said ten. Last week you sat right there and told me ten with a perfectly straight face.
I was younger when I said it. The core in this housing keeps worse time than I do, and it's running down faster than either of us bargained for.
That was yesterday.
It was a difficult night. They're all difficult now — I've only stopped mentioning the ones that don't manage to surprise me.
You could have told me it was four. I'd have come sooner. I'd have come every day.
Theron took up a narrow chisel.
No.
Theron set the blade against the stolen fragment.
Put the chisel down. That piece is evidence. It's the one proof we have that the stone did a thing stone has no business doing.
Evidence of what, exactly? We haven't even got a name yet for the thing it did.
We don't know yet. Which is precisely why you don't go carving pieces off it before it's finished telling us.
I know what happens to you without it. I've watched it happen. I'm not going to stand in this workshop and let the proof come to matter more than the man who's keeping it.
…Then be quick about it, and quiet. And Theron — keep the shavings, every last one. If this is going to cost you, I want it written down somewhere that it did.

He tapped once. A thin shaving broke free, bright enough to light the lines of his palm. Timinny looked toward the shuttered window, jaw tight — not grateful, never that, because gratitude would mean admitting the necessity. Theron removed the exhausted core and fitted the shaving into its place. Color spread slowly through the contacts, and the tension around Timinny’s mouth eased.
The density's wrong. The Crown fragment carries more charge than its mass should allow. Either our instruments are lying, or the stone's drawing strength from somewhere else.
From the storm, you think — drawing the charge down out of the air itself?
Perhaps. Or from the other pieces still in the ground.
Theron looked at the three-point brace around the model tower. Timinny followed his gaze.
A single block strengthens what touches it. An arrangement redirects force across distance. If the underground formations do the same…

He left the thought unfinished. Outside, Fulminary was mining those formations faster with every season. Edenite healed lungs, arrested infections, and kept storm walls standing — and each new disaster raised the demand for the very mineral whose absence might be making the disasters worse.
Record everything at the Crown. Heat, vibration, position. And don't decide what it means before it happens.
And when Varrik catches me holding a gauge to the wall instead of a pick — what exactly do I tell him?
Tell him an engineer ordered it.
Are you an EMC engineer, Timinny? Because he will ask, and he'll know full well your name isn't on any list he's obliged to respect.
No.
Then that's unlikely to help me, and rather likely to earn us both a long conversation with the Commission.
Timinny handed him a compact gauge made from copper prongs and a scratched glass dial.
Then be useful. Useful enough, and often enough, that letting you go stays the more expensive choice. It's how I outlasted my own legs.

At the door Theron glanced back. Timinny had already turned to the model tower, sketching a circle around its three braces; for the first time that morning he looked not ill but alive with a question. The wrapped fragment flashed. Thunder answered several heartbeats later.

Crownvein Mine was less than a year old and already too important to fail. Its staging floor had been carved into the western ridge beneath Sturmvale — a vaulted cavern crowded with timber lifts, wet rails, hanging lamps, and enough workers to populate a village. Ore carts passed beneath the stamped crest of the Edenite Mining Commission. Clerks weighed every load behind barred windows. From there the stone rose into a city that needed it for medicine, for reinforcement, and for the increasingly difficult business of remaining where it had been built.
Theron joined the western crew at the tally board.
Your mother — breathing any easier these days? My eldest still asks after her. She's not forgotten the bread Bethella used to send down the shaft.

Joren Vale had spent twenty-two years underground and claimed it gave him seniority over certain mountains. Square-faced and broad through the shoulders, he wore three differently colored threads around his wrist — one for each of his daughters.
On the quiet days. The storm days she spends teaching me not to fuss over her, and that takes most of the wind she's got.
Joren glanced toward the shaft, where dust trembled from a support beam though no cart was passing.
A quiet day. You let me know if you ever turn one up down here — I've been looking twenty-two years and come up empty.

On Theron’s other side, Pell tightened the strap of a new helmet whose leather had not yet learned the shape of his head. It was his third week at Crownvein, and he still checked every buckle twice whenever an experienced miner might be watching.
Western face today. They're saying the vein down there runs thick as a city wall — that a man could work it a year and never once reach the back of it.
People say a great many things before they go down. Most of it turns modest again on the way back up.
Theron.

The voice crossed the staging floor like a thrown tool. Foreman Varrik stood beside the tally board — a hard-built elf with iron-gray hair cut close to the scalp and a face weathered into permanent disapproval. Crownvein was the largest mine under a single foreman’s authority, a fact he wore less like an honor than a siege assignment. Every missed quota reached the Commission under his name. Every injury did too, though the quotas seemed to trouble him more.
Theron stopped in front of him. Varrik waited.
Foreman.
When a foreman says your name on his own floor, the answer he's owed is 'yes, foreman' — not the sight of you standing there measuring the silence like it's worth something.
Didn't want to interrupt.
You got the western face because someone above me mistook patience for talent. So you'll cut, you'll load, and you'll keep your clever hands out of your pockets.
Theron felt the hidden weight of Timinny’s gauge inside his satchel.
In that order?
Quota's doubled — and doubled before the storm arrives, not after — so spare me your arithmetic when you're standing at the bell wondering how.
Doubled because of the storm?
The retaining walls need reinforcing. The infirmaries need treatment stone. Every frightened councilor's finally learned what keeps his ceiling over his head.
And pulling twice as much out from under it — you've thought that part through, have you, or only the part where the carts come up full?
Varrik’s chalk stopped.
Is the work.

choices.choice_text: "Understood."
tags: outcome:Theron swallows the warning. Varrik hears obedience and nothing else.

choices.choice_text: "The western braces are carrying a vibration that isn't on the load chart."
tags: impact:Make Varrik alert despite his hostility
outcome:Varrik rejects Theron's conclusion, but the warning lodges beside every vibration he feels afterward.

choices.choice_text: "If the ceiling comes down, I'll count whatever lands in the carts."
tags: outcome:The crew hides its laughter. Varrik does not, and he remembers exactly who caused it.

scenes.title: The Last Ordinary Shift
scenes.subtitle: The western extraction face
scenes.author_notes: Fixed events: first anomaly, mine collapse. visual_brief: An immense curving vein of luminous Edenite dominating a deep gallery; one miner down near the vein; Theron between the wounded worker, a dark-threaded fragment and a fissure producing impossible knocks. Three visibly competing priorities. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

entry_effects.notice: Side quest begun: No One Left Below

blocks.content: The cage lift swallowed twelve miners and began its descent. Sturmvale vanished above them one platform at a time — pale constructed walls giving way to black native stone, slick with runoff. The air warmed. Lamps swung from the cage roof, and each gallery opened briefly beyond the bars: workers at pumps, carts on sidings, EMC inspectors in clean coats trying not to touch anything.
Does the pressure in your ears ever let up? Mine have been full since the second platform down.
Yes. Once they burst.
Pell paled.
He's lying, Pell. They don't burst. They only stop complaining once you've stopped listening for them.
Mostly.

At the western level they followed new rails into a gallery bright with reflected blue-white light. The Edenite formation surfaced first in scattered seams, then widened until it curved through wall and floor in a nearly continuous arc. It was indeed thick as a city wall. It was also familiar — Theron had seen its shape that morning, in the blank crescent on Edran’s map. The workers mistook his stillness for awe. Varrik mistook it for delay.
Positions.

Theron crossed to a support and laid his palm against it. The timber hummed beneath his skin. Three pulses. A pause. Three more. He slipped Timinny’s gauge from his satchel and pressed its copper prongs to the stone; the needle climbed past the final marking and quivered there. Varrik raised one hand. Along the face, miners lifted their tools.
Foreman—
Varrik dropped his hand. The first strike landed. Every lamp in the gallery dimmed. Far beyond the exposed face, something answered.

The quota turned the gallery into noise. Steel rang against wedges. Cart wheels shrieked along wet rails. Tallymen shouted weights over the rhythm of a dozen tools biting into stone, and the great Edenite arc caught every spark and returned it as cold blue light. Beneath all of it, Theron heard the knocking. Three impacts. A pause. Three more. Not within the gallery. Behind the Edenite.

He moved along the face with the gauge concealed against his forearm. The needle swung hardest near the center of the arc, where Pell and Joren were setting an extraction wedge. Theron checked the support spacing, then checked it again. The loads were within Commission limits. The stone said otherwise.
Pell. Leave that one.

The younger miner looked to Varrik before he looked to Theron. That moment of hesitation was enough. Joren’s hammer struck the wedge. A section of Edenite split from the arc with a sound like ice breaking across a winter lake. Thunder rolled through the floor and up Theron’s bones — and only afterward sounded in the sky above. The hair along every miner’s arms lifted.
Stop cutting.
Hold the line.
That charge isn't in the vein at all — it's coming up from below us.
Secure the cut.

Pell raised his hammer again. The metal head flashed white and burst at the socket. The broken shard spun across the gallery, tore through his thigh, and struck the wall hard enough to spark. He fell without a cry. For half a heartbeat nobody moved. Then blood spread over the pale dust beneath him and touched the raw edge of the exposed vein.

The Edenite brightened. Pell arched from the ground — the gash in his leg drawing itself closed, flesh joining flesh in a smooth line. A murmur of astonishment passed through the crew. Then the wound opened again. Thin red branches spread outward from it, dividing across his skin in patterns that did not follow the path of the shard. His hands clawed at the stone.
It's pulling.

Near Theron’s boot a piece of the broken formation rolled free — a black filament running through its brilliant center, the twin of the fragment in Timinny’s workshop. Behind the wall, the measured knocking accelerated.

Three needs presented themselves at once: Pell bleeding on the floor, the impossible sample already fading in the dust, and the hidden source of the sound moving closer. Theron had time to choose only one.

choices.choice_text: Drag Pell away from the vein and bind the original wound.
choices.description: Theron reaches the wounded man first. The fragment and the fissure will have to wait.
tags: outcome:Theron chooses the bleeding miner. Pell reaches safety, while the fragment and fissure disappear into the emergency.

effects.notice: Pell is clear. Someone is still trapped below.

choices.choice_text: Wrap the dark-threaded fragment before its glow fades.
choices.description: The other miners will move Pell — but the delay will cost him.
tags: outcome:Theron preserves the impossible sample. Behind him, other hands reach Pell later than his could have.

choices.description: Each knock moves toward the spike until the metal taps by itself.
tags: impact:Alert the mine to structural danger
outcome:The marking spike taps without a hand on it. Theron leaves with a route no ordinary survey could have found.

scenes.title: A Room Without an Entrance
scenes.subtitle: Beneath Crownvein
scenes.author_notes: Fixed event: unmapped space exposed. visual_brief: An ancient-looking void exposed behind luminous stone, not a constructed temple. Smooth black boundaries interrupting natural strata; scorched mineral veins like roots; Theron among collapse debris with one or two miners; weak sickly Edenite glow. No recognizable religious symbols, no fully visible demon. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

entry_effects.notice: Quest updated: Map the impossible chamber

blocks.content: Dust streamed from the ceiling in pale curtains.
Away from the face!

The order came late, but it came. Miners abandoned their tools and caught hold of Pell; Joren shouted for a litter. Theron looked toward the lift tunnel — and the hanging lamps between them and the shaft winked out, one after another.
Order the lift — now, while there's still a lift left to order.
You don't give orders on my floor, Theron. Not today of all days.
Then borrow mine. Call them your own if it helps — just get them moving.

The entire Edenite arc went dark. Silence struck the gallery harder than thunder. In the sudden black, something enormous pressed against the far side of the stone, and the wall bowed inward. Miners screamed. Timber supports snapped in sequence. Theron saw Varrik turn toward the crew, saw Joren throw himself across Pell, saw a line of blue fire race through the floor beneath his boots. Then the western face folded. He fell through cold light and black dust; stone struck his shoulder, his lamp vanished, and for several breathless seconds there was no direction — only weight and the roar of a mountain rearranging itself. He hit solid ground, and darkness closed over him.

When Theron opened his eyes, his lamp was burning several paces away, its flame lighting a low chamber of smooth black stone. No drill marks scored the walls. No timber braced the ceiling. Beyond the wall, very faintly, someone spoke his name.
Theron?
It was Edran’s voice exactly — not an imitation, not a stranger with the same pitch. And Edran was miles away, in the EMC archive.

Theron rises in a chamber that should have been solid. The walls are neither cut nor natural. Stone appears to have drawn away from a central emptiness. Scorched veins reach outward, stopping wherever intact Edenite remains.
The wrapped fragment pulls toward the black wall.
Theron immediately recognizes the exposed boundary as the edge he traced.
The wounded miner's words repeat in Theron's memory: something under it.
A trapped miner calls from beneath a fallen brace. Another lamp moves in a side hollow.
Theron. You left me below.
Edran doesn't sound that dramatic. Edran can barely manage dramatic when he's trying.
The voice shifts into Bethella's cough.
Most of the crew had pulled back from the face before it gave way. Fewer are trapped down here than there might have been.
The collapse caught the whole face crew. Somewhere in the dark, the injuries are worse than anything Theron can count from where he stands.

choices.choice_text: Follow the airflow, not the voice. Free the trapped miner.
tags: outcome:Theron follows the honest airflow and reaches the miner before the chamber can finish closing around him.

effects.notice: Side quest completed: No One Left Below

choices.choice_text: Follow the scorched veins to where the black boundary meets a fresh extraction line.
tags: impact:The trapped miner pays for the delay
outcome:Theron stays with the pattern long enough to understand part of the seal. The cry behind him changes while he is drawing.

effects.notice: The trapped miner could not wait.

scenes.title: The Living Route
scenes.author_notes: Branch of C03-A; reconverges at S07 after one scene. visual_brief: optional — a narrow break in collapsed stone, cold air, lamp light on a hand-like impression forming inside solid rock. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: Theron wedges a broken support beneath the trapped stone.
Leave me. The wall's moving — I can feel it deciding, and it isn't deciding in our favor.
Walls are slow. You're complaining fast. Between those two speeds I like our chances — now give me your arm.
He frees the miner and follows cold air through a narrow break. Behind them, the impossible chamber collapses, burying most visible proof.
The rescued miner sees a hand-like impression form briefly inside solid rock.
I saw it. Whatever you want to call it — I saw it move where there was no room left to move.
Then hold onto that. Keep it clear in your head for the day some important man in a clean coat stands in front of you and explains that you didn't.

choices.choice_text: Put the miner's arm over your shoulders and carry him every step to daylight.
choices.description: Do not ask an injured man to spend strength proving what happened.
tags: outcome:Theron carries the miner into daylight. The man will remember that he was treated as a life before he was treated as evidence.

choices.choice_text: Make him repeat exactly what he saw before shock can soften the memory.
choices.description: Turn a terrifying memory into a record the Commission cannot dismiss as easily.
tags: outcome:The miner repeats the impossible detail three times. By the third, it has become testimony instead of panic.

choices.choice_text: Mark the cold-air route and sketch the surviving edges of the chamber before leaving.
choices.description: Trade a few dangerous minutes for a route and geometry you may need later.
tags: outcome:Theron leaves a return mark no ordinary collapse should erase and carries a rough geometry into the next argument.

scenes.title: The Hollow Pattern
scenes.author_notes: Branch of C03-B; reconverges at S07 after one scene. visual_brief: optional — notebook geometry sketched by lamplight, scorched paths ending at intact Edenite. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: Theron scratches the chamber geometry into Timinny's notebook. Every scorched path ends at intact Edenite. Every opening aligns with an extracted section above.
Record everything.
Theron holds his lamp closer. A shape moves where no space exists.
A cry cuts through the chamber. Theron returns to the trapped miner, but the shifting brace has crushed one leg. Theron frees him, unable to undo the injury.
You were right there. You had your hand out to me. And then you didn't, and I've been telling myself it was the dark.
Theron has no answer that helps.

choices.choice_text: Tell the miner the truth: you chose the pattern before you chose him.
choices.description: Honesty cannot restore his leg, but it can refuse the easier lie.
tags: impact:Repair part of a damaged bond
outcome:The miner does not forgive Theron. He does stop wondering whether the darkness invented the abandonment.

choices.choice_text: Seal Timinny's notebook inside your coat and memorize the most important curve.
choices.description: Make certain the injury was not paid for with evidence that can still be lost.
tags: outcome:The notebook survives beneath Theron's coat. The curve in his memory refuses to become an ordinary circle.

choices.choice_text: Crush the smallest resonant splinter until the borrowed voice loses its hold.
choices.description: Sacrifice a piece of evidence to reduce the thing's purchase on your thoughts.
tags: impact:Give up part of the evidence
outcome:The splinter breaks with a sound like an unfinished name. For the first time since the chamber, Theron's thoughts are entirely his own.

scenes.title: Lines That Should Meet
scenes.subtitle: Bethella's home, that night
scenes.author_notes: Fixed event: Edran maps barrier geometry. visual_brief: Night inside the family home; mine dust still on Theron; Edran overlaying official surveys with Theron's rough chamber sketch; Bethella nearby as rain intensifies; luminous map lines forming a broken underground ring. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: Bethella cleans a cut above Theron's brow.
The messenger from the EMC stood on our step and called it equipment failure. He had it all written down, so I suppose that's meant to settle it.
Equipment did fail. Every word of that is true. It's only the order of things they've got wrong.
Theron.
The wall failed first. Before any tool, before any man — the wall. They wrote down the second thing and left the first one in the dark where they found it.
You've hidden a truth inside a true thing so nobody has to look straight at it. I taught you that. I'd only hoped you'd spend it on smaller matters than this.
Edran studies Theron's sketch, turning it twice.
The sketch is thin — a shape remembered while running.
The notebook pages are dense with measured angles, taken while a man was still trapped behind him.
This bend's wrong. I've redrawn it four times thinking my hand slipped, and my hand doesn't slip four times in exactly the same place.
It isn't your hand and it isn't the bend. It's the room. The room is wrong, and your line's only being honest about it.
Rooms can be built badly, I'll grant you that. But stone can't sit at this angle and still meet the western descent — not on its own, not without a hand putting it there.
It doesn't meet it. It surrounds it.

Edran overlays the old Crownvein survey. The blank curve joins Theron's chamber line. Together they suggest a wide ring of dense Edenite around a central void. New extraction marks have cut through it.

choices.choice_text: "You've got enough to correct the map. Leave the rest to me."
tags: impact:Shield Edran from the worst truth
outcome:Theron gives Edran the geometry and keeps the voice. Edran notices the shape of what has been withheld.

choices.choice_text: "Something spoke from the wall. It used your voice. That missing curve isn't an error."
tags: outcome:Edran hears exactly how his voice was used below. Fear enters the room, but secrecy leaves it.

choices.choice_text: "I've been taking fragments. Timinny and I have been testing them. And something down there used your voice."
tags: outcome:Theron lays every secret on the table. Edran is angry, frightened, and finally working from the whole map.

scenes.title: Grounding the Storm
scenes.subtitle: Timinny's workshop, heavy rain
scenes.author_notes: Fixed event: Timinny helps prove grounding. Opens with the C04 payoff and Bethella's question from S07. visual_brief: The workshop during heavy rain; Edran's ring map beneath a circular arrangement of Edenite fragments and copper contacts; Timinny directing from his chair; dark motion inside one fragment; electrical light bending through the ring. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

entry_effects.notice: Quest updated: Test the grounding theory

blocks.content: You came home last night talking around every answer, like a man walking the long way round a hole he'd rather not fall into.
So I'll ask it plainly, and you can circle all you like: what was behind that wall?
Good. I was worried you'd come up with a sensible reason.
If that stone was holding something down all this time, then answer me one thing — why would the Council ever stand up and order you to dig it out?
Because no one ever told them it was holding anything. You can't protect a wall nobody knows is load-bearing.
Then we tell them. Tonight, before they cut it any thinner than it already is.
Lightning silently illuminates the windows.
Timinny compares the ring map to the three-point model.
He has already reproduced Theron's results on his own, and steps in as a full partner without being asked.
He makes Theron reproduce each claim in front of him before he will accept the ring model.
He calls Theron out for hiding where the fragment came from, and only then agrees to go on.
A brace carries weight because every point in it agrees where the weight should go. Take one point out of that agreement and the whole thing stops being a brace and starts being a warning.
So the seam was never only ore.
It was ore. That is what makes it hard — a thing can be useful and still have had a purpose long before we touched it.
Edran has left his copied map on the bench, but not himself — he is nowhere in sight.
It isn't flat — I checked it twice and then a third time to be sure. The northern edge rises, the whole length of it, toward Sturmvale.
Like a channel.
Or a circuit.
A circuit someone laid down and then buried — and we've spent a generation mining the insulation off it and calling the sparks weather.

They place fragments at the mapped elevations. Timinny charges the model. The first attempt cracks a support. The second sends charge into the wrong wall. Theron rotates the darkest fragment so its natural grain points back toward the ring.
On the third attempt, light travels around the entire model and grounds through the base. The storm outside weakens for one breath.
Then every fragment turns toward Theron.
Open.

choices.choice_text: Knock the central contact free.
tags: outcome:Theron breaks the circuit before it can take more from Timinny. The safe reading is incomplete, but both men remain standing.

choices.choice_text: Keep a hand on the contact while Timinny records the flow.
tags: outcome:Theron holds the contact through one final pulse. Timinny captures the complete return path, and the charge leaves something behind.

scenes.title: A Miner Before the Commission
scenes.subtitle: EMC hearing chamber
scenes.author_notes: Fixed event: Orsik rejects warning. Opens with the S08 risk payoff. visual_brief: A severe administrative chamber of polished dark stone, EMC insignia, quota ledgers and guarded Edenite displays; Theron dusty and plainly dressed before elevated officials; Orsik controlled and socially distant, never overtly monstrous. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: Sensible.
Don't sound so disappointed.
The word OPEN repeated through Theron's bones until Timinny shouted him off the contact. A faint branching burn remains on his palm.
The ring didn't strengthen the model. That's the part I keep coming back to.
It told the force where to go.
And Crownvein cut clean through the instructions without ever knowing they'd been written.
Then take the Council your evidence, before Varrik carts off the rest.
A miner backs up the account of the impossible wall, then loses his nerve under questioning.
The fragment stirs in answer to the Edenite stored in the chamber, and Orsik turns even that against him: contaminated, stolen material, nothing more.
Theron lays out his sketches and Edran's map. The officials call them interpretations, not proof.
Timinny's measurements demonstrate abnormal grounding. They do not demonstrate demons.
Theron admits to the experiments himself, before Orsik can spring them for effect.
Orsik produces the custody discrepancy with no warning, and the room belongs to him after that.
The injured miner appears as a witness, thin and upright and stubborn about what he felt pull at him.
Orsik points to the man's condition as proof that Theron delayed the rescue, or mishandled the scene, or both.
I was there. I chose the wall over the man. Say the rest of it, Commissioner — I won't contradict you.
You're asking the Commission to close the most productive mine in Fulminary because a wall spoke to you in your brother's voice.
I'm asking you to stop cutting for one season — long enough to understand what the Edenite was actually doing down there before we take the rest of it out.
We understand it well enough to heal your injured men, brace your mother's roof, and keep half this city standing.
Then explain why the storms get worse every time the carts get heavier.
Correlation spoken confidently is still correlation.
And a collapse called equipment failure is still a collapse.
The custody discrepancy is laid on the table.
You've removed undeclared Edenite from Crownvein.
Yes.
Repeatedly.
Yes.
You conducted unauthorized experiments with an unlicensed engineer, and now you present the results as cause to halt national production.
The results are true no matter how little you think of the people who found them.
That sentence is the first evidence you've offered against anything but yourself.
Orsik refuses to order a shutdown. Extraction will continue — now under EMC inspection.

choices.choice_text: "Send your inspectors. Let me show them the chamber before another cut is made."
tags: outcome:Theron accepts the Commission's process and its watch. His evidence receives a hearing; Crownvein receives no warning yet.

choices.choice_text: "If you won't stop the cut, then the workers deserve to know the truth."
tags: outcome:Theron abandons the room and gives the warning to the people who must survive it. The Commission answers with guards.

effects.notice: The miners hear the warning the Commission withheld.

choices.choice_text: "Its purpose was to find out whether the facts were going to be expensive."
tags: outcome:Theron refuses to spend another minute making truth acceptable to the Commission. He leaves to make it useful.

scenes.title: Under Watch
scenes.author_notes: Branch of C05-A; reconverges at S11 after one scene. visual_brief: optional — an EMC side chamber, storm readings climbing on a wall gauge. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: Theron waits in an EMC side chamber as storm readings climb. The floor vibrates in groups of three.
Edran turns up with the finished ring survey and will not leave until a clerk sets it beside the fresh subsidence reports.
Timinny sends a mechanical recorder carrying a repeated charge spike from Crownvein.
An official opens the door.
Commissioner Veyr has authorized your transfer to the mine.
Transfer?
He didn't say release.

choices.choice_text: Accept the escort—but make the official carry Edran's survey into the mine.
choices.description: Let the Commission believe it is still in control while putting your evidence inside its chain of custody.
tags: outcome:Theron enters the transport under guard. Edran's survey enters beside him under an official seal no clerk can later pretend not to recognize.

choices.choice_text: Slip Timinny's recorder to Edran and tell him to take it to the eastern grounding point.
choices.description: Risk the record to place a working instrument where the city may soon need it.
tags: outcome:The recorder leaves beneath Edran's coat while the official is still explaining transport protocol. The plan now exists outside the Commission room.

choices.choice_text: Jam the side door with a survey spike and leave before the escort can form.
choices.description: Give up the Commission's protection and take responsibility for reaching Crownvein yourself.
tags: impact:Reach the streets without an escort
outcome:The spike bends, the latch holds, and Theron is halfway into the rain before procedure discovers it has been left behind.

scenes.title: The Bell Without Leave
scenes.author_notes: Branch of C05-B; reconverges at S11 after one scene. visual_brief: optional — the shift bell, miners gathering in confusion, guards arriving late. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: Theron reaches the shift bell before EMC guards reach him. He sounds the emergency pattern. Miners gather in confusion.
The western face is unstable — the ring beneath it is broken and it's carrying a charge that isn't on any chart. Keep everyone out of the lower cut until it's been inspected.
You don't command this mine. You don't command so much as a lamp in it.
Then command them somewhere safer.
Some miners obey Theron because of the earlier collapse. Others wait for Varrik.
Varrik remembers the earlier warning and quietly holds the deepest crew back — even as he curses Theron aloud for ringing the bell.

choices.choice_text: Spend your head start assigning partners, shelters, and names to every lower-cut team.
choices.description: Make survival specific before the guards turn the warning into a debate.
tags: outcome:By the time the guards reach the bell, every lower-cut miner has a partner and a route. Panic has become a plan.

choices.choice_text: Make Varrik repeat the shutdown order where the whole shift can hear him.
choices.description: Turn a hostile foreman into a public part of the record.
tags: impact:Force Varrik to acknowledge the danger
outcome:Varrik repeats the order through clenched teeth. Forty miners hear him choose caution, and that fact cannot be put back inside his mouth.

choices.choice_text: Open the restricted store and take every intact Edenite segment the crew can carry.
choices.description: Break Commission custody now so the mine has something to rebuild with later.
tags: outcome:The restricted-store lock lasts one hammer strike. The crew carries out enough intact Edenite to make disobedience useful.

scenes.title: Back Through the Rain
scenes.author_notes: Branch of C05-C; reconverges at S11 after one scene. visual_brief: optional — copper leads, setting hammers and survey pins gathered by lamplight while rain hammers the workshop roof. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: Theron and Timinny gather copper leads, setting hammers, survey pins, and every usable Edenite remnant in the workshop.
Edran works beside them, marking elevations as they are packed.
This isn't a device. It's an argument made out of scrap.
The Commission preferred the other kind of argument. The kind that comes stamped.
Edran discovers the plan and insists on bringing the missing elevation map.
You can protect me after we survive.

choices.choice_text: Use the remaining minutes to finish Timinny's grounding harness.
choices.description: Trust the warning already given and make one piece of the solution reliable.
tags: outcome:The last copper return closes cleanly. What began as an argument made of scrap becomes a tool Theron is willing to carry underground.

choices.choice_text: Split the maps and experiment record into three waterproof packets.
choices.description: Accept less equipment in exchange for evidence no single arrest or collapse can erase.
tags: outcome:Edran takes one packet, Timinny hides another, and Theron seals the third beneath his shirt. The truth no longer has a single throat to cut.

choices.choice_text: Send Edran through the workers' alleys with names, routes, and the warning the Commission refused to issue.
choices.description: Divide your group and preparation to give Crownvein's families time to act.
tags: outcome:Edran vanishes into the workers' alleys carrying a warning measured in names instead of statistics. Doors begin opening ahead of the storm.

scenes.title: Sturmvale Bends
scenes.author_notes: Fixed event: storm and breach unify. Protected-character rule: Bethella survives. visual_brief: Sturmvale under a supernatural storm; blue-white charge crawling through structural Edenite; stone buildings bending or fracturing; Theron and Edran moving Bethella toward shelter; Timinny navigating rain-slick streets in his engineered chair; the storm centred beneath the city rather than above it. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: The storm arrives from below.
Every Edenite brace in Sturmvale flashes at once. Charge climbs walls, leaps between roofs, and returns toward Crownvein.
Bethella collapses as stormlung steals her breath. Theron supports her while Edran clears a route.
Go to the mine.
You can't breathe.
And you can't lie convincingly. The mine, first.
I can get her to the eastern shelter.
You don't know what's happening.
Because you decided I shouldn't.
The ring rises beneath the shelter district. If the southern point fails, the charge comes here next.
Timinny arrives with the grounding assembly. His treatment housing flickers as the city's Edenite supply destabilizes.
Crownvein isn't a mine anymore. It's the break in the circuit.
The eastern shelter, Timinny's failing housing, and Crownvein's blue-lit road pull in three directions. Theron has time to choose one.

choices.choice_text: Carry Bethella to the eastern shelter yourself. The mine can wait for one promise kept.
choices.description: Guarantee your mother's safety, but reach Crownvein after the first wave of the storm.
tags: outcome:Theron chooses the weight in his arms over the disaster on the horizon. Bethella reaches shelter because he carries her there.

choices.choice_text: Trust Edran with Bethella and keep Timinny's treatment housing alive long enough to finish the ground.
choices.description: Protect both engineer and equipment while placing your mother's route in Edran's hands.
tags: outcome:Edran takes Bethella east. Theron turns toward the failing machine and makes the solution survive the storm.

choices.choice_text: Send Bethella and Timinny to shelter together. Take Edran's map and run for Crownvein before the next discharge.
choices.description: Leave the people you love to protect one another so you can confront the source before it worsens.
tags: impact:Reach Crownvein before the next discharge
outcome:Theron places the map inside his coat and runs toward the blue horizon. Behind him, his family closes ranks without waiting for permission.

scenes.title: A Promise Kept
scenes.subtitle: The family road
scenes.author_notes: Agency branch: Theron personally secures Bethella before the descent.

blocks.content: Theron carries Bethella through streets that bend a finger's width each time the ground flashes.
You always did mistake worry for a debt.
Tonight I can afford to pay one.
He waits until the shelter door closes and hears Bethella strike it twice from inside—the family signal for safe.
Crownvein discharges again before Theron reaches the mine road. The delay is real. So is the promise he did not break.

scenes.title: The Grounding Run
scenes.subtitle: The maker's road
scenes.author_notes: Agency branch: Theron saves Timinny and completes the grounding preparation.

blocks.content: Theron braces Timinny's chair beneath a stone awning while charge crawls over every exposed copper lead.
The treatment relay or the grounding return. I cannot keep both closed.
Then stop treating them as two circuits.
Theron bridges the housings through an Edenite clasp. Timinny's breath evens as the grounding coil takes a clean blue charge.
That is either brilliant or medically insulting. Bring it back so I can decide.

scenes.title: Before the Sirens
scenes.subtitle: The breach road
scenes.author_notes: Agency branch: Theron reaches Crownvein early and turns warning into preparation.

blocks.content: Theron reaches Crownvein before the city sirens find their rhythm. The staging yard is still deciding whether the blue light is weather.
Pairs. Chalk your partner's name inside your cuff. If a familiar voice calls from an empty shaft, you do not answer it alone.
The miners obey because Theron gives them verbs instead of reassurance: pair, mark, brace, wait.
You are giving orders in my yard.
Then arrive in time to improve them.

scenes.title: The Descent Against Orders
scenes.author_notes: Fixed event: first incursion occurs. The two closing choices are the supported representation of the conditional VARRIK_STANCE update (shaken, or cooperative when the crew was warned); exactly one is ever available. visual_brief: Crownvein's entrance during catastrophic weather; overturned carts, crooked lifts, blue lightning travelling down into the mine; a lesser demonic form partially manifested from stone and smoke — undeniable but unstable, asymmetrical, hard to comprehend. Not a generic horned humanoid. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: You caused a panic, stole Commission stone, and came back carrying a workshop toy.
Then the day's still full of surprises.
I didn't believe your ghosts. I believed the braces.
Varrik stays hostile, but the miners who always liked Theron's mouth make room for him anyway.
A miner strikes what appears to be a collapsed support.
The support unfolds.
It has no stable anatomy. Stone passes through a body made of smoke, wet sinew, and absence. It moves only where the Edenite ring has been cut.
Varrik attacks it with an extraction tool. The tool passes through until its Edenite edge flashes, forcing the creature back.
That's not a ghost.
I'll try not to look pleased.
Two knocks sound from the shelter relay: Edran's confirmation that Bethella is safe. Theron lets himself hear it once, then turns toward the descent.
The completed grounding harness hums against Theron's ribs. Timinny's survival and the working circuit have become the same advantage.
The Crownvein crews are already paired and marked. Theron's choice to run ahead has converted the first minutes of disaster into preparation.
The route splits: trapped crew in the lower gallery, broken ring segments near the breach, and an unstable grounding path through the upper supports.

choices.choice_text: Take the split routes with Varrik at your shoulder.
tags: impact:Descend with Varrik as an ally
impact:Prepared crews open a coordinated route
outcome:Varrik falls into step beside Theron. The alliance is late, hostile, and real enough to carry underground.
choices.author_notes: Crew was warned at the bell: Varrik becomes cooperative.

choices.choice_text: Take the split routes while Varrik is still deciding what he saw.
tags: outcome:Theron takes the split route without waiting for Varrik's certainty. The mine closes behind him one decision at a time.
choices.author_notes: Crew unwarned: Varrik is shaken rather than cooperative.

scenes.title: The First Incursion
scenes.author_notes: Fixed event: climax priority selected. visual_brief: split Crownvein galleries — a folding lower gallery, a broken luminous arc near the breach, and failing central supports strung with copper. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

entry_effects.notice: Quest updated: Survive the first incursion

blocks.content: Three routes, one man, and a mine that is finished pretending to be a mine.
Below, the trapped crew. Ahead, the broken ring. Above, the grounding path that Timinny sketched and nobody has tested.

choices.choice_text: Reach the lower gallery before it folds into the breach.
choices.description: Edran's elevations give Theron a ventilation cut the maps do not show.
tags: impact:Leave the seal in critical condition
outcome:Theron spends the remaining route on people. The lower gallery empties while the best surviving proof disappears behind it.

choices.choice_text: Return salvaged fragments to the broken arc.
choices.description: Each restored segment narrows where the entities can move.
tags: outcome:Theron returns preserved knowledge to the barrier. Every seated fragment takes a corridor away from the incursion.

choices.choice_text: Climb the failing central supports and lay Timinny's copper path.
choices.description: A path toward the surface discharge point, if the supports hold.
tags: outcome:Theron carries Timinny's work over the failing supports. The current gains a route upward, and the dark gains another moment inside him.

scenes.title: The Seal That Was Taken
scenes.author_notes: Fixed events: seal restored, Theron survives, stormscar created. The two closing choices are the supported representation of the conditional VARRIK_FATE resolution; exactly one is ever available. visual_brief: Theron in the impossible central chamber amid a broken circular network of Edenite; salvaged fragments, copper conductors and mine supports forming an improvised grounding system; a vast presence pressing behind thinning stone without being seen; lightning coursing through Theron, leaving branching dark mineral scars along arm and shoulder. ASSET UNRESOLVED.

entry_effects.notice: Quest updated: Reconstruct the Edenite seal

metadata.alt: The trapped crew carried up through the ventilation cut.
The Edenite ring restored across the broken gallery.
The grounding route secured, alone, against the incursion.

blocks.content: Every path reaches the central chamber. Varrik remains behind to hold a failing gate while Theron enters.
You wanted the cut stopped.
I wanted you to stop it.
Take what you can get.
Most of the lower crew came up through the ventilation cut. Some did not, and nobody had time to learn their names.
The rescue was handed to other hands while Theron worked the arc.
You build doors.
Today I'm closing one.
The chamber is larger than before, because less of the barrier remains.
The Presence uses familiar voices in succession: Bethella, Edran, Timinny, then Theron's own.
They take from you. Open, and be more.
I've met important men. You sound just like them.
Theron identifies three surviving ring points. The extracted Edenite in his pack is not enough to rebuild the original barrier, but it can reconnect the remaining structure.
The copper path is ready and waiting.
One connection has to be improvised with whatever came down in the pack.
There is no cable left. There is an extraction tool, and there is his body.
The northern point's higher than where you are. The map was wrong.
Your map or theirs?
Theirs.
I knew there was a reason I liked yours.
Don't brace against the force. Give it a path.
A path where?
Somewhere that isn't us.
Theron redirects the circuit through Crownvein's central supports and toward exposed bedrock beyond Sturmvale.
The ring reconnects. Every loose fragment rises from the chamber floor and turns toward the gap. The lesser entities lose shape. The Presence strikes the barrier from below.

Theron closes the final connection with his hand. Storm charge passes through his arm, shoulder, and chest. Dark branching marks form beneath his skin. He remains conscious long enough to rotate the last fragment with its grain aligned to the ring.
The chamber contracts. The extracted galleries collapse inward, burying Crownvein's richest deposit back into the seal. The storm discharges across uninhabited western stone rather than Sturmvale.

choices.choice_text: Wake in rain that falls normally.
tags: outcome:Theron wakes to ordinary rain and Varrik's ragged breathing. The man who gave the order has survived to answer for it.
choices.author_notes: Varrik is pulled from the failing gate with a crushed arm and survives.

choices.choice_text: Wake in rain that falls normally.
tags: impact:The survivors inherit his final order
outcome:Theron wakes to ordinary rain and an empty place where Varrik's argument should have been. The surviving miners carry the last order instead.
choices.author_notes: Varrik holds the gate until the last miners pass; the collapse takes him before Theron emerges.

scenes.title: Thunder Moving East
scenes.author_notes: Fixed events: local containment, Eden Tower insight seeded, threat moves east. The aftermath, family resolution, official resolution, Eden Tower seed and eastward-storm image are all ordinary narrative blocks so the run cannot finish before them; the ending record then adds its epilogue. visual_brief 1: a damaged but standing Sturmvale after the storm, Crownvein sealed in the distance, Theron bearing a dark branching stormscar, Edran supporting him, Bethella and Timinny rejoining them. visual_brief 2: Theron's sketch of connected elevated Edenite structures. visual_brief 3: unnatural storm clouds moving east across the continent. ASSETS UNRESOLVED.

blocks.content: You look terrible. I mean that with all the love I've got — you look like something the mine spat back up because it didn't care for the taste.
Accurate maps inspire confidence. You always did draw an honest line.
Edran grips his unscarred hand.

metadata.alt: Family aftermath: the reunion in a damaged but standing Sturmvale.

blocks.content: Varrik is carried out with a crushed arm and an expression that dares anyone to comment on it.
Varrik does not come up. The last miners through the gate describe a man who did not move from it.
Bethella touches the edge of Theron's scar without touching the darkest lines.
Does it hurt?
Only when I breathe.
Theron.
Yes.
Does it hurt?
Yes.
She rests her forehead against his.
Timinny goes through Theron's notes. His deepvein treatment took a knock in the disruption, but he is steady enough to keep arguing.
You rebuilt a continental barrier with mine scrap.
Crownvein scrap.
Stolen Crownvein scrap.
It returned itself.
Orsik meets Theron without the elevation of the hearing chamber.
The Commission will record an unknown subterranean event and an emergency structural intervention.
You saw what came out.
I saw what the public can survive knowing today.
Crownvein failed after unauthorized interference with Commission property.
He saved the city.
History requires evidence.
No. Records require evidence. History happens regardless.
Put my statement in the record. Theron warned me before the first collapse. I ordered the cut anyway.
Orsik cannot fully bury the account.
Surviving miners repeat both Theron's warning and Varrik's final act, to anyone who will stand still for it.

Later, Theron sits in Timinny's workshop with his scarred arm supported in a sling. Edran's ring survey lies beside the three-point tower model. Theron sketches multiple elevated structures connected across a landscape.

metadata.alt: The first tower sketch — a concept, not yet built.

blocks.content: More seals?
Not below.
Towers?
Paths. If the storm can be told where to leave one city, maybe it can be told to stay out of the rest.
That'll take more Edenite than you can fit in your pocket.
Then I'll need a better pocket.
Crownvein was closed. Sturmvale stood. The High Council called the disaster contained.

Far beyond Fulminary, shepherds watched birds abandon the western sky. Wells warmed in villages that had never heard the word Edenite. Along roads leading east, travelers carried stories of thunder beneath clear weather.
Theron had closed one wound.
The land had begun to open elsewhere.
An unnatural storm front moves from west to east across the distant continent.

metadata.alt: Thunder moving east: an unnatural storm front crossing the continent.

blocks.content: What was carried out of Crownvein
The seal below Sturmvale holds — locally, and only locally.
Theron carries a stormscar down his arm and shoulder.
Bethella reached shelter and breathes.
Theron carried Bethella to shelter himself. She remembers the promise he chose to keep.
Theron trusted Edran with Bethella's life. Both reached the eastern shelter.
Timinny was caught in the open streets when the charge climbed the walls, and reached shelter on his own wheels.
Theron stabilized Timinny's treatment housing and carried a completed grounding plan into Crownvein.
Timinny sheltered with Bethella. Theron trusted them to keep one another alive while he ran for the breach.
Timinny's treatment was disrupted but he is alive and still arguing.
Varrik lives, one arm crushed.
Varrik did not come up.
The injured miner from the western face recovered.
The injured miner from the western face is in a critical bed, and the ward will not promise anything.
The miner Theron left beneath the brace lost a leg.
The warned crew came up in numbers that surprised everyone.
The crew went down unwarned, and the casualty list is longer than the record will admit.
Part of the crew received Theron's warning. Preparation saved lives, but not every gallery heard in time.
Theron's measured notes survive.
Only a rescued man's word survives.
Whatever proof there was went down with the galleries.
A rescued miner's repeated statement survives as evidence instead of rumor.
Theron's field rubbing preserves the shape of a chamber the collapse erased.
The evidence entered official custody before the disaster. The Commission cannot deny receiving it.
Forty miners remember the shutdown order in the same words.
Three copies of the record survive in three different hands.
Edran knows only what a map can be made to say.
Edran knows about the voice in the wall.
Edran knows all of it, theft included.
Timinny trusts Theron completely.
Timinny still checks Theron's work twice.
Timinny has not forgotten what Theron withheld.
Theron's exposure to the seam is minor.
Theron has been in the charge more often than any body should be. Something in him answers weather now.
Theron became a Guardian: the kind of hero who measures victory by who is still there to argue afterward.
Theron became a Seeker: the kind of hero who carries an unwelcome truth farther than fear can bury it.
Theron became Defiant: the kind of hero who refuses to let authority decide which dangers are permitted to be real.
Theron became a Maker: the kind of hero who builds an answer while everyone else is still defining the problem.
The Commission's record will say the disaster was contained. Far to the east, the land has not read the record.
